title: Jamelle Holieway: The Freshman QB Who Won the 1985 Title
question: Who was the freshman quarterback on Oklahoma's 1985 national championship team?
answer: Jamelle Holieway, a true freshman from Los Angeles, took over at quarterback after Troy Aikman broke his leg against Miami in October 1985 and guided the Sooners to a 25-10 Orange Bowl win over Penn State and the national title.
summary: Jamelle Holieway was a true freshman when he replaced the injured Troy Aikman and led Oklahoma's wishbone to the 1985 national championship. Here is his story.
body: When Troy Aikman broke his leg in Oklahoma's October 1985 loss to Miami, the Sooners turned to a freshman from Los Angeles. Jamelle Holieway (OU 1985-88) had been a standout at Banning High School in Wilmington, and Barry Switzer handed him an offense built around the wishbone. According to the Sooner Stats game recap, he became the starter in the fourth game of the season.

He made the most of it. Holieway led Oklahoma in rushing in 1985 with 861 yards, a rare feat for a quarterback, and kept the wishbone humming as the Sooners ran the table afterward. In the Orange Bowl on January 1, 1986, Oklahoma beat top-ranked Penn State 25-10 to claim the national championship. His own rushing line that night was modest, but he delivered one huge moment: a 71-yard touchdown pass to tight end Keith Jackson.

Holieway is widely described as the first true freshman starting quarterback to lead a team to a national title. He stayed at the controls through 1988, earned first-team all-Big Eight honors in 1985 and 1986, and finished his OU career with 2,713 rushing yards and 32 rushing touchdowns, according to Wikipedia and Storming the Norman.

After Oklahoma he went undrafted in 1989 but played for the Los Angeles Raiders and then the BC Lions of the CFL. Sooner fans remember him less for the pro stops than for a fearless freshman year that gave Oklahoma its sixth national championship.
